chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'He who awakens in the morning not being concerned with the affairs of the Muslims is not a Muslim.'

key_terms.فَلَيْسَ بِمُسْلِمٍ: so he is not a Muslim

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be concerned with the affairs of the Muslims according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the concept of *al-ghammah bi umur al-muslimin* (concern for the affairs of the Muslims) as a core pillar of communal identity. It elevates passive belief to active stewardship, implying that indifference to the collective welfare constitutes a deficiency in one's faith. This principle is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for understanding individual responsibility (*taklif*) within the broader social and political context of the Ummah.
